In a purely competitive market, the price of a good is naturally driven to the value where the quantity demanded by consumers matches the quantity made by producers, and the market is said to be in equilibrium. These values are the coordinates of the point of intersection of the supply and demand curves.  (a)  Given the demand curve p −50 2 1 20x and the supply curve p −20 1 1 10x for a good, at what quantity and price is the market for the good in equilibrium?  (b)  Find the consumer surplus and the producer surplus when the market is in equilibrium. Illustrate by sketch- ing the supply and demand curves and identifying the surpluses as areas. 9.  The sum of consumer surplus and producer surplus is called the total surplus; it is one measure economists use as an indicator of the economic health of a society. Total surplus is maximized when the market for a good is in equilibrium.
